grammarFocus: have to / must / can；一般现在时与过去时对比。
title: A Busy Week at the Office
instructions: 听录音，完成10个问题。录音会播放两遍。第一遍听大意，第二遍听细节。答案必须来自录音原文。填空题答案必须与原文完全一致，且不超过字数限制。所有题目均为单选题或填空题。
transcript:
M: Hi, Lisa. How was your week?
W: Busy! I had to work late on Monday and Tuesday.
M: Oh no. Why?
W: My boss gave me a big report. I must finish it by Friday.
M: That's tough. Do you have to work this weekend?
W: No, I don't. But I can't relax yet. I have to check the numbers first.
M: I see. Did you have meetings yesterday?
W: Yes, I had a meeting at nine o'clock. It lasted thirty minutes.
M: Thirty minutes? That's short.
W: Yes, it was quick. But I must prepare for the next one on Thursday.
M: Can you take a break now?
W: Not really. I can drink coffee, but I can't leave the office.
M: You work too hard. Last year, you didn't have to work late so often.
W: I know. But this month is different. I have to train a new colleague too.
M: Really? Who is it?
W: His name is Tom. He started last week. He must learn our system fast.
M: Good luck. I hope you can rest soon.
W: Thanks. I must go now. The report is waiting!

grammar.title: have to / must / can; 一般现在时与过去时对比
grammar.explanation: have to 表示“不得不”，must 表示“必须”，can 表示“能够”。一般现在时表示经常或现在的情况，一般过去时表示过去的情况。例如：I have to work late today. I had to work late yesterday.
grammar.example: I have to check the numbers first. I had a meeting at nine o'clock.

questions.explanation: 主语是第三人称单数，have to 变为 has to。must 后直接跟动词原形，不加 to。
can 是情态动词，后面直接跟动词原形，不加 to，也不用 -ing 形式。
Yesterday 表示过去，动词用过去式 had。
must 后跟动词原形，不加 -s 或 to。

part1: Do you have to work late often?
What must you do at work or school?
Can you take a break when you are busy?
Did you have a busy week last week?
speaking.part2: Describe a busy week you had. You should say:
part3: Do you think people have to work too hard today?
What must students do to succeed?
Can time management help people relax?
How did people manage time before computers?

transfer.writing: Write a short paragraph (5-6 sentences) about a busy day you had. Use have to, must, can, and the past tense. Example: Last Monday, I had to finish a report. I must check the numbers. I can drink coffee, but I can't leave the office.
